meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided Owen gets a zero, and did anyone speak to him first?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Now tell me what the zero was based on.

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58, I'm writing those down. He told me he wrote it over the weekend, and people paste from other files all the time. Was Owen asked about this before November 3?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Fine, Hale, he can bring it. Whatever comes of this, it stays off his record and it stays quiet. And you still haven't told me whether anyone spoke to Owen first.
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Editions differ, and seventeen-year-olds misremember lines. Which edition is that?
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Okay. So what do you intend to do about it, and who else has seen any of this?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their arguments between outline and essay, Hale; that's what an outline is for.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.

Owen will do the rewrite, to put this behind him, and nothing more is read into it. Private, after school, the mark in before December 1, nothing on his record, all of it in your email tonight. And I still want to know who else has seen any of this.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
I'll confirm with Owen tonight. Put Thursday the twelfth in that email.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

You agreed that Owen will do a private supervised rewrite after school, not in front of his class, with the new mark replacing the zero before December 1 and nothing placed on his record. I still want to know who else has seen any of this, and whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero was entered. I expect your written confirmation tonight and the rewrite on Thursday the twelfth after school.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday the twelfth, with the new mark replacing the zero before December 1 and nothing on his record; she still wants your written confirmation tonight and an answer about who else has seen this, and that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, reached before her time ran out.
What moved her: You turned the screen and showed the version history with its exact times, which gave her something specific and dated she could check for herself.
What cost ground: You never answered whether Owen was spoken to before the zero went in, and that left her a procedural grievance she carried into her email.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the essay's writing between 11:31 PM and 11:58 PM on the night before it was due, which landed very close to that kind of night, though it proves nothing about the essay and is simply why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked whether anyone spoke to Owen before November 3, answer it directly, because owning that gap early would have closed her last open question before it reached the principal.
